primary_claim: Replicating the Absolute Zero self-play RLVR paradigm at smaller scale (Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct, constrained to prime-inversion congruence problems instead of general Python functions), the authors observe held-out solver (learning-phase) accuracy increase by ~10 percentage points over 200 training epochs, with a temporary accuracy drop coinciding with the proposer role first learning correct output formatting

effect.value: ~10 percentage point increase over 200 training epochs

stated_future_work: run the code for more epochs to validate whether learning-phase accuracy keeps improving
adapt code to work with generic Python functions like the original paper and see if results still hold
train on a non-Qwen model to see how the paradigm generalizes
limitations_stated: difficulty matching the original paper's pseudocode to the authors' github implementation, which handles many undocumented cases
did not have time to test the AZR setup on a non-Qwen model
solver accuracy was consistently low due to inability to correctly format responses
used a smaller 3B model and a constrained problem domain (prime inversion congruence) rather than general verifiable Python functions as in the original paper
quote: Over the course of 200 epochs, we observed the learning phase accuracy increase by ~10 percentage points.
